title: Strategy Signal Blueprint and Cross-Team Commitment Triage
creator: Omar Singh
description:
Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable framework ("Strategy Signal Blueprint") that maps quarterly company-level strategy signals to a prioritized set of initiatives and produces a cross-team commitment triage output for the cycle planning meeting.

Problem: Current company OKR->initiative translation is inconsistent across orgs. PMs and Eng often over-commit or under-communicate dependencies, leading to scope churn mid-cycle and missed outcome targets. We need a structured input->decision flow that is lightweight enough for PLG cadence but rigorous enough for enterprise commitments.

Scope:
- Define 3–5 canonical 'strategy signals' for the quarter (e.g., Cost per Token reduction target, Latency 95th SLO, Dedicated capacity uptake, Private deployment enterprise pilot).
- Create mapping templates that connect each strategy signal to candidate initiatives, required teams, rough effort band, and gating criteria.
- Introduce a cross-team 'Commitment Triage' process that:
  1) captures firm vs aspirational asks,
  2) identifies hard dependencies and single-threaded owners,
  3) surfaces regressions vs previous cycle OKR signals, and
  4) outputs a prioritized commitment slate for exec sign-off.
- Produce artifacts: a Confluence blueprint, a CSV/graph of dependencies for the planning workshop, and a one-slide commitment slate for leadership.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template and blueprint published to Confluence (link in comments).
- At least 8 candidate initiatives mapped across 4 strategy signals for 2026-Q2.
- Cross-team triage session run with Eng, Product, Design, and Infra; documented decisions and owners in the dependency graph.
- Exec-ready commitment slate created and approved by Strategy & GTM leads.

Output format:
- A single Confluence page with: overview, template, example filled mapping, triage checklist, RACI matrix.
- Dependency export (CSV) and a lightweight graph (PNG) attached.

Rationale and trade-offs:
- Keep the mapping at the signal->initiative level (avoid deep task-level planning) to preserve agility.
- Use a pragmatic scoring rubric (impact to signal, customer-facing visibility, dependency risk, effort band) to auto-sort candidates; scoring will be intentionally coarse (1–3) to avoid false precision.

Rollout plan:
1) Draft blueprint & scoring rubric (owner: Lina) — complete by 2026-03-10.
2) Run 1st cross-team triage workshop (owners: Lina, Eng leads) — target 2026-03-18.
3) Iterate with org leads and produce commitment slate — target 2026-03-25.
4) Leadership sign-off and publish — target 2026-04-01.

Metrics to measure success:
- % of initiatives in-cycle with clear owners and dependency resolution plan (target >90%).
- Reduction in mid-cycle priority shifts caused by undisclosed dependencies (target 40% drop vs prior quarter).
- Executive satisfaction with commitment slate (qualitative sign-off).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-engineering the rubric. Mitigation: Keep scoring 1–3 and limit signals to 3–5.
- Risk: Missing single-threaded owners for infra-heavy work. Mitigation: Hard gate — no commitment without an owner.

Notes on tooling:
- We'll store the mapping CSV in Drive and the canonical blueprint in Confluence. The dependency graph will be generated from the CSV via a small Graphviz script (repo link in comments).

Deliverables:
- confluence.redwood.com/display/STRAT/Strategy+Signal+Blueprint+2026-Q2 (draft)
- drive.google.com/drive/folders/strategysignals-2026-q2 (mapping CSV + exports)
- github.com/redwood-inference/strategy-scripts (graph export script, PR referenced in comments)

Longer-term: If adopted, the blueprint will be iterated into a console-friendly 'initiative registry' that product and platform teams can use to attach runtime metrics and rollout windows to commitments.
